title: Nutshell: Update tools-and-toolsets doc to use tools= (toolsets key is unsupported)
description:
Tactus-in-a-Nutshell has guidance that suggests using agent_config.toolsets = {...}. In current Tactus DSL, Agent does not support a 'toolsets' key; tool/toolset references live under 'tools'.

Files to update:
- ../Tactus-in-a-Nutshell/chapters/06-tools-and-toolsets.qmd

Acceptance:
- Remove/replace any recommendation or examples that use toolsets = {...}.
- Replace with canonical: tools = {"filesystem_tools", done} or tools = {"filesystem", done} (server/toolset name strings), plus Toolset "..." { use = "mcp.<server>" } when appropriate.
- Ensure examples match current semantics: Toolset is a bundle; Agent.tools accepts tool + toolset references and transformation dicts.
creator: Ryan Alyn Porter

custom.beads_close_reason: Updated Tactus-in-a-Nutshell tools/toolsets chapter to remove Agent.toolsets and pushed
custom.beads_notes:
Outline / writing notes:

- Problem: This chapter documents Agent{ toolsets = {...} } but the DSL rejects 'toolsets'; use Agent.tools instead.

- Target mental model:
  - Toolset = named bundle of tools.
  - Agent.tools = list of tool/toolset references + optional transformation dicts.
  - MCP servers register toolsets by server name when configured in .tac.yml; you can also alias them via Toolset "x" { use = "mcp.<server>" }.

- Concrete replacement snippet (keep it short):

  Toolset "filesystem_tools" {
    use = "mcp.filesystem"
  }

  local done = require("tactus.tools.done")

  file_manager = Agent {
    provider = "openai",
    model = "gpt-4o-mini",
    system_prompt = [[Use filesystem tools. When done, call done.]],
    tools = {"filesystem_tools", done},
  }

- If you want to show per-turn restriction, keep it in the Agents cheat-sheet style:
  worker({tools = {}}) -- no tools this turn
  worker({tools = {"filesystem_tools", done}})

- Remove/replace these exact lines in ../Tactus-in-a-Nutshell/chapters/06-tools-and-toolsets.qmd:
  - 'Use toolsets = {...} for string-named tools ...'
  - the example block that uses toolsets = {"filesystem_read_file", ...}

- Optional addendum (1-2 sentences): In mock mode, MCP toolsets may be placeholders; real tool execution requires MCP config.
